transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Thursday, November 26. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Want Akhilesh as UP CM, but won't settle for less than 100 seats: Congress. Congress MP Imran Masood expressed doubts about the intentions of Samajwadi Party during ongoing seat-sharing negotiations. The discussions, which lasted 3.5 hours, were complicated by SP's announcement of five candidates, causing tension. Masood emphasized that Congress seeks a significant number of seats for the 2027 elections while supporting Akhilesh Yadav for CM. SP leaders dismissed Masood's concerns as personal and affirmed no formal objections were raised. Watch: FedEx aircraft runs off runway at Miami airport on Thanksgiving eve. A FedEx cargo aircraft overran a runway at Miami International Airport on Wednesday night, forcing the temporary closure of all but one runway on the eve of Thanksgiving. No injuries were reported. The FAA will investigate the incident, which comes nearly three months after an Amazon cargo plane overran another runway at the airport, killing five people. How Rajasthan Royals missed once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to acquire Hardik Pandya. Rajasthan Royals had a chance to land Hardik Pandya, a proven IPL-winning captain and an all-rounder, but balked at Mumbai Indians' demand to include Jofra Archer in the trade. While RR stuck with Riyan Parag, Punjab Kings seized the opportunity, trading Arshdeep Singh for Hardik in a blockbuster piece of business. Tata Sons seeks public status ahead of IPO; Noel opposes Chandra reappointment, EGM move. Tata Sons is looking to make changes to its articles of association in anticipation of an upcoming initial public offering. Additionally, N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as executive chairman will be proposed at an extraordinary general meeting. However, Noel Tata, leading the Tata Trusts, is contesting these actions as he focuses on his merger ambitions. Both meetings encounter quorum issues, with outcomes regarding the amendments and reappointments expected before the IPO filing. Nvidia AI chips flood the market and the reason is US rule aimed at China. New US measures have triggered an increase in Nvidia AI chips on the market, targeting Chinese companies' access to high-tech computing hardware. These restrictions explicitly bar the direct sale of Nvidia's leading GPUs to businesses in China. As a result, sellers are eager to liquidate Nvidia chips originally set aside for Chinese clients, tightening the reins on loopholes that allowed remote access to US AI technology. 'Gambhir, just look at how he is hitting': WC-winner's message on Sooryavanshi. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hammered 204 off just 53 balls for India A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars, bringing the debate over his promotion to the senior Indian team back into focus. Japanese creator says life feels inconvenient after returning from India. A Japanese content creator shared her reflections on returning home after an extended stay in India. She observed that daily life in Japan felt less convenient, particularly due to the lack of numerous app-based services that she had grown accustomed to. The creator highlighted how vital delivery apps were during her time in India, sparking conversations on social media about the effort and costs associated with such conveniences. What Trump's new 25 percent tariff threat with a 17 percent trade deal rate means for India. The Donald Trump administration's move assumes significance because the India-US trade deal is yet to be finalised. Up to 25 percent tariffs on all goods from India, net of existing Section 301 tariffs, with exemptions for certain goods would be applicable, but there is also the prospect of 17 percent tariffs if a trade deal is agreed on. Watch: DMK recreates 'Theri' scene, hangs TVK MLA's effigy over harassment case. DMK student wing members hung an effigy of TVK MLA C Arul Vignesh from a bridge in Vandavasi, Tiruvannamalai district, on Thursday, demanding his arrest over a sexual harassment complaint filed by a woman district collector. Customer wins rupees 1 lakh as travel platform's mixed messages cause duplicate bookings. A consumer commission in Punjab has ordered Cleartrip and its CEO to refund rupees 80,340 to a customer named Parminderjeet Singh Khurana. The commission found that contradictory booking messages caused Khurana to mistakenly reserve the same flight tickets twice. After receiving no clear assistance about his payment status, Khurana rebooked the trip, resulting in duplicate charges. Additionally, the commission awarded him rupees 20,000 for the distress caused.

transcript.text: Next, science and technology. Apple to launch its seventh India store in Hyderabad on December 10, here's what customers can expect. Apple will open its first Hyderabad retail store, Apple Kukatpally, on December 10 at Lake Shore-Y Junction Mall, taking its India store count to seven. Customers will get access to Apple's latest products, expert support and free Today at Apple creative sessions. Now Google's Familiar Faces AI feature works on Walmart's $35 smart home camera too. A couple of Walmart's budget-friendly smart home cameras will be able to recognize people around your house now using Google's familiar face detection feature. A new Google Home update brings Familiar Faces support to the $35 Onn Outdoor Camera Plug-In and $77 Onn Floodlight Camera Hardwired. However, a Google Home Premium subscription is still required S and P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance and 'key man' risks. The credit rating agency may lower Nvidia's credit rating to AA-, the fourth-highest rating. Scientists discover mysterious lakes more than a mile beneath the Red Sea. More than a mile beneath the surface of the Red Sea, scientists have discovered rare underwater lakes that could reveal secrets about Earth's ancient oceans and the possibility of alien life. Known as brine pools, these extremely salty, oxygen-free environments are surprisingly teeming with microbial life, challenging our understanding of where living organisms can survive. Nothing Ear (note) design revealed ahead of 8 December launch: AI recording, transcription and TALK buttons confirmed. Nothing has revealed the design of its Ear (note) AI earbuds ahead of the 8 December launch, showing a metallic charging case with dedicated TALK and RECORD buttons. The earbuds are expected to support AI-powered call recording, meeting transcription, summaries and Hi Amazon loses its latest attempt to get out of handling more recall notices. Amazon is on the hook to recall more than 400,000 hazardous products after losing its legal battle against the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). The US District Court for the District of Maryland ruled in favor of the CPSC, which argued that Amazon is a distributor of goods, not a logistics provider, making it FCC approves SpaceX plan to put AI data centers in space. The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority. World's largest trial of robotic knee replacement reveals surprising results. Robot-assisted knee replacement surgery offers greater surgical precision, but a landmark clinical trial has revealed a surprising limitation. Despite the advanced technology, patients experienced no meaningful improvements in pain, mobility, or recovery compared with conventional surgery after one year. Google's patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment's future. Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that's designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users. The patent has been rejected, but unfortunately, Google might appeal or resubmit an amended version, and we could see this monstrosity come OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work. OpenAI will introduce a single usage meter across ChatGPT as it combines the Chat and Work experiences. Scientists discover a surprising twist in how the body burns calories. Researchers have discovered that a drug can significantly increase the body's energy expenditure without clearly activating calorie-burning brown fat. The unexpected finding reveals a new challenge in developing obesity treatments that harness the body's natural fat-burning machinery. HONOR Magic 9 Pro Max debuts in Malaysia with dual 200MP cameras and cinematic ARRI video technology. The HONOR Magic 9 Pro Max is positioned as a flagship device targeting photography enthusiasts and content creators, with the company highlighting its low-light imaging capabilities, advanced stabilisation, professional colour processing and video recording features. Jensen Huang broke Nvidia's code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it. Most codes of conduct serve as a reflection of corporate culture. In Nvidia's case, that could have consequences. Common sleep and anxiety drugs could be harming aging brains. Nearly one in three older adults with dementia or other cognitive disorders takes potentially harmful medications that can worsen brain function and increase the risk of hospitalization and premature death. Despite encouraging progress over the past decade, researchers warn that medication-related harm remains a major and potentially preventable threat to healthy aging. Motorola Edge 70 Neo versus Vivo S2 versus Nothing Phone 4a: Which offers more for rupees 40,000?. Motorola Edge 70 Neo takes on Vivo S2 and Nothing Phone 4a in India. Compare their prices, processors, displays, batteries and cameras. WhatsApp's new scheduled messages let you choose the right time to send. WhatsApp's 3 billion users are getting an option that Meta says is one of the most requested features, with the ability to schedule messages in advance for both private conversations and group chats. Most messaging platforms have had this for a very long time, but now it's on WhatsApp too. If you think of a The canceled Tesla Cybertruck is the fastest-selling used truck in America. The Tesla Cybertruck was the fastest-selling used truck last month, averaging just 39.1 days on the market compared to 65.5 days for trucks overall. A space telescope hunting for dark matter just discovered something unexpected. ESA's Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, despite being designed to study distant galaxies and the mysteries of the dark Universe. The icy object is approximately 1.3 billion kilometers from Earth and follows an unusual orbit that takes thousands of years to complete. Apple iOS 27 versus Samsung One UI 9: Which smartphone software offers better performance, AI and multitasking?. Apple's iOS 27 focuses on faster performance, an improved Siri and ecosystem integration, while Samsung's One UI 9 offers greater customisation, multitasking and Galaxy AI features. Here's how the two smartphone operating systems compare and what users should consider before choosing. EPA reports 'zero' airborne lead following controlled Army detonation in Iowa. Saying it was necessary to prevent the possible spontaneous explosion of a stockpile of material used in igniters and blasting caps, the US Army conducted a controlled detonation of over 9,700 pounds of lead azide today at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa. Videos of the detonation showed plumes of smoke several Anthropic's Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI 'absurd'. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pushes back against rivals' accusations that he favors surrendering human agency to AI, even as leading AI companies increasingly automate their own research and model development. Physicists trap antimatter in a breakthrough that could explain why the universe exists. Positrons are the antimatter counterpart of an electron. Physicists trapped a positron and cooled it to temperatures near absolute zero. Positron is suspended in a wall-free trap, safely separated from ordinary matter. Team will conduct most precise comparison yet between matter and antimatter. Google, Meta risk fines up to 5 percent of global revenue: Inside Australia's new law to curb harmful online content. Australia has passed the Digital Duty of Care law, requiring Google, Meta and other major platforms to proactively tackle harmful online content or face fines of up to 5 percent of their global revenue.

transcript.title: Development and policy
transcript.text: Now to development, infrastructure and government policy. Cabinet approves India-Singapore MoU to boost aviation MRO skills and infrastructure. Inside India newsletter: Roaring economy, foreign investors' return and now record auto sales. Sarvam Token Factory controversy: Why India needs clearer rules for sovereign AI and subsidised compute. Indian economy stands out amidst uneven global performance: RBI. PM chairs 55th PRAGATI meeting. Modi's Criticism of India Inc. Puts Weak Investment in Focus. SAMHiTA Project : Strengthening India-Sri Lanka Cultural Ties. Cabinet approves rupees 11,000 crore Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem. Reforms to Expand Foreign Participation in G-Secs. India bans sugar exports with immediate effect until September 2026.

transcript.title: Across India
transcript.text: Turning to the big national stories. 'Could be something good': NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule strikes softer tone on delimitation Bill. NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule struck a softer tone on the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, saying her party would examine its provisions and support it if it served the country's interests. She said opposing every government proposal was not necessary. Sule also dismissed speculation about her party joining the NDA or her getting a ministerial berth as "gossip". A commitment to strengthen our Constitution. On Constitution Day, the Prime Minister underscores the pivotal role of the Constitution in shaping Indian democracy and society. He elaborates on various steps taken toward fostering social justice, economic parity, and inclusivity through government initiatives. The article reflects on key amendments enhancing constitutional rights and their benefits for marginalized groups, while also tackling historical governance issues. FIR against comedian Yash Maheshwari over alleged remarks on Bihar women and Chhath festival. Delhi Police has registered an FIR against stand-up comedian Yash Maheshwari over alleged objectionable remarks about women from Bihar, the Chhath festival and the tradition of applying sindoor. Chemistry most popular subject after English for 12th CBSE students. In 2027, the CBSE has achieved an impressive milestone with 19 lakh candidates registering for Class 12. An encouraging trend reveals a marked rise in science registrations, notably in chemistry, physics, and mathematics. Notably, the disparity between chemistry and business studies has skyrocketed since 2019. This surge aligns with a national educational shift, showcasing a clear preference for science over commerce fields. 'Zero tolerance for terrorism': EAM Jaishankar remembers 26/11 victims on attack anniversary. External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Thursday paid tribute to the victims of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, remembering the innocent lives lost and the security personnel who made the supreme sacrifice while fighting the terrorists. 7th high court posting? Justice Rao may be Karnataka Chief Justice. Justice M S Ramachandra Rao has been recommended for the position of Chief Justice of the Karnataka high court. This potential appointment would mark his seventh high court assignment since 2012 when he became a judge. He has previously served as Chief Justice in four high courts over a short period. Justice Rao has experienced multiple transfers throughout his judicial career due to various circumstances. Thirupparankundram Deepam row: Tamil Nadu governor Rajendra Arlekar seeks explanation from TVK govt. Tamil Nadu governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar has sought an explanation from the TVK government over the alleged non-compliance with a Supreme Court directive to light the traditional Karthigai Deepam at a stone pillar atop the Thirupparankundram hill in Madurai, official sources cited by news agency PTI. 'Fighting against BJP or us?' Congress slams Samajwadi Party over its list. Congress MP Imran Masood expressed doubts about the intentions of Samajwadi Party during ongoing seat-sharing negotiations. The discussions, which lasted 3.5 hours, were complicated by SP's announcement of five candidates, causing tension. Masood emphasized that Congress seeks a significant number of seats for the 2027 elections while supporting Akhilesh Yadav for CM. SP leaders dismissed Masood's concerns as personal and affirmed no formal objections were raised. Lamp not lit atop deepathoon, Supreme Court to hear contempt case. The Tamil Nadu government has not complied with the Supreme Court's order regarding the Karthigai Deepam lamp lighting. This non-compliance may trigger contempt proceedings against the Madurai Collector, despite his apology. Various political parties and the Madurai district administration oppose the lighting of the lamp atop the deepathoon. The Collector reported efforts to follow the Supreme Court's directive, which were ultimately unsuccessful. India tops in videos removed from YouTube. YouTube took down approximately 34.4 lakh videos from India in the second quarter of 2026. This number represented a 28 percent increase from the previous quarter's removals. Globally, child safety issues were responsible for the majority of video removals. Additionally, Indian courts and government agencies sent numerous removal requests to Google. 4 from Keralam among 11 Indians killed in UAE bus accident. Four people from Keralam are among 11 Indians who were killed when a bus rammed into a truck parked along a road in the UAE's Ras Al Khaimah early Tuesday. 'Priceless legacy': PM Modi pays tribute to Ambedkar, Constituent Assembly on Constitution Day. Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday greeted citizens on Constitution Day, remembering Dr BR Ambedkar and other members of the Constituent Assembly for their role in framing the country's Constitution. 'Our artists bringing new perspectives to art world': PM Modi after Venice Biennale award. The India Pavilion received the Visitors' Lion Award for Best National Participation at the Venice Art Biennale. Curated by Amin Jaffer, it featured five contemporary artists exploring themes of memory and migration. Prime Minister Narendra Modi acknowledged this achievement as a significant moment for India's cultural landscape. The pavilion returned to Biennale Arte after a seven-year gap, showcasing diverse Indian perspectives and heritage. Meta officials meet Congress over suspended accounts. In New Delhi, Meta representatives held discussions with Congress social media officials amid growing complaints about account suspensions and content deletions affecting the opposition. Supriya Shrinate raised critical concerns about what she deemed interference by Meta in political issues. In response, the officials clarified that they strictly comply with Indian content laws and maintain their stance of political impartiality throughout these processes. Delhi to Dhaka: Probe minority attacks, Hasina passport a separate issue. In response to escalating violence against minorities in Bangladesh, India has expressed its serious concerns, urging the government there to conduct an extensive investigation. The Ministry of External Affairs noted the unique circumstances surrounding Sheikh Hasina's passport and extradition request, highlighting that these matters are being processed according to established protocols. Furthermore, two Indian nationals suffered injuries in a recent Houthi assault in Riyadh, prompting a strong condemnation from India. Bail to be granted under UAPA when there is delay in trial, says Supreme Court. The Supreme Court has confirmed that its authority to grant bail cannot be overridden by stringent laws. It ruled in favor of a government doctor who has been jailed for over four years. Additionally, the Court granted bail to senior officials involved in a significant corruption case in Rajasthan. These decisions highlight ongoing tensions in bail jurisprudence amid contradictory orders from different benches. Exporters in better position but brace for uncertainty. Indian exporters are adapting to potential tariffs from the United States while they finalize a trade agreement. The impact of these tariffs may create temporary uncertainty for exporters as they manage future orders. Current strategies involve rushing shipments to avoid increased costs before the new tariffs kick in. Exporters believe that negotiating a reduced tariff rate will provide a competitive advantage in the market.

transcript.title: Around the world
transcript.text: And finally, here is what is happening around the world. Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu. The Israeli PM says his trial should end after judges said there was little chance of conviction in one of three cases. FedEx plane overshoots Miami runway, with flights briefly suspended at airport. The brief ground stop comes on the day before the US Thanksgiving holiday, one of the busiest travel days of the year. Macy's postpones Thanksgiving parade due to severe weather. The was the first time ever that the iconic celebration was delayed because of storms. New York expects damaging winds and heavy rainfall over the Thanksgiving holiday. North Korea expels Swiss diplomat in sanctions row. Swiss officials said relations would be kept through North Korea's embassy in Bern, and its own embassy in Beijing. My family were killed in Ukraine. My mum blamed Zelensky's troops - the truth is complicated. BBC journalist Anastasiya Gribanova investigates who killed her father and grandparents in the war. Russia's own figures show it has lost nearly 500,000 people in Ukraine war. Leaked data reveal how the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has fundamentally changed mortality patterns in Russia. Israeli strike kills senior Hamas security official and family in Gaza City. Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, head of Hamas's internal security service in northern Gaza, was killed with his wife and two teenage daughters, doctors say. Five Russian military jets hit in airfield strike, says Ukraine. The Savasleyka airfield hosts aircraft used by Russia to launch hypersonic missiles and glide bombs at Ukraine. Protesters call on Israel to free Palestinian student held without charge. Mahdi Tunsi, 26, was taken from his university dormitory earlier this month and has since been held without charge.

transcript.title: Sign-off
transcript.text: That is your briefing. Stay sharp, and have a strong day.
